correctness.rationale: The known strict-weight vertex description is correctly specialized. The double-multiset squared-distance bound is attained only on complementary balanced supports and yields exact pair counts. Strong convexity forces a unique center, permutation symmetry gives the scalar center, and rank increment signs give one/two adjacent contacts. Geometric-sum and uniform convergence arguments establish all three asymptotic regimes with correct normalizations. The included runnable exact-arithmetic verifier passed 165,555 vertex pairs, 41,644 rank inequalities, 495 independent profiles and eight large-n asymptotic checks; none is substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text Joswig–Klimm–Spitz (2021, Sections 2–4) establishes the SIM-polytope vertex orbits and generalized permutahedron but does not state the projected Euclidean diameter, general outer ball, complete contact locus, or three geometric-discount entropy regimes. Doker (2011), the SIM auction origin, and full HTML of Behrend et al. (2022) were separately checked for relevant metric assertions. A close published indexed special-family circumball result was compared implication-wise: its arithmetic-profile classification cannot determine arbitrary strictly decreasing weights or the geometric-discount limits. Novelty remains provisional because that indexed result was not available in full text.

value.rationale: A natural and established n-parameter generalized-permutohedron family has exact Euclidean diameter and outer-ball/contact geometry for arbitrary strict weights. The geometric-discount deformation reveals three sharply distinct natural contact-count entropy scales while combinatorial types remain fixed, an interpretable phenomenon not a trivial renaming or arbitrary finite search. The concise diameter inequality is valuable principally when combined with the complete contact classification and multiscale asymptotics.
